third_party_cartridges.summary: No report found that firmware blocks third-party toner on the B230 itself. A Xerox B235 service manual (sibling model on the same platform) describes a 'non-Xerox supply detected' warning that can be bypassed by a key sequence; this is a search excerpt, not a page I could open. One Xerox.ca owner blames a chip for blocking cheaper cartridges (single anecdote).

windows.why: Xerox publishes Windows 10 and 11 drivers and the built-in IPP driver works, but owners and one reviewer report Wi-Fi setup trouble on the small screen and a setup failure with Xerox's recommended print system.
windows.driver: Xerox full driver packages from support.xerox.com: PCL6 V4 7.249.0.0 (Jan 2022, lists Windows 10 x64 and Windows 11) and generic PPD 5.810.0.0 (Jul 2021, lists Windows 10 and 11, no Windows on ARM). Windows 11 also offers the inbox Microsoft IPP class driver. Xerox says newer devices are no longer added to its Global Print Driver.
problems: ITPro reviewer: Xerox software failed with the recommended Type 4 Print System; Type 3 worked
Wi-Fi password is hard to enter on the small LCD, at least during first setup
Reports of Wi-Fi disconnects and having to re-enter passwords (one comparison article)
Unofficial help sites describe 'offline' status after Wi-Fi setup (not confirmed for B230)

sources.what: PCL6 driver 7.249.0.0 (Jan 2022): Windows 10 x64 and Windows 11 listed; no ARM

Review: Type 4 Print System failed in test, Type 3 worked; no other Windows issues mentioned
Owner reviews: Wi-Fi password entry on small screen, setup confusion at first

forums.why: Owners praise reliability, wireless use, two-sided printing and no subscription, but repeat complaints about Wi-Fi setup, toner cost and one very costly support case.
praise: Reliable, few problems (switchers from HP say so)
Wireless and phone printing work well
No subscription; Linux and Chromebook support
Good print quality once toner darkness is raised
complaints: Wi-Fi password setup hard on the small screen
Wi-Fi connection problems, some owners want Ethernet
One reviewer cites 260 USD of tech support to get it working (same review twice)
Paper feed pulls several sheets at once and jams at the back (one review)
Prints a scanner report several times a day with no way to stop it (one review)
Starter toner rated only about 750 pages in one report

sources.what: 10 visible of 27 ratings; all show 5 stars but text is mixed; praise for reliability and wireless, complaints about support cost and paper feed; Wi-Fi password setup
10 reviews: praise for Wi-Fi, reliability, two-sided; complaints about toner cost, gibberish prints, support, scanner report
Editorial review: 'excellent value' for black text; running cost about 2p per page for toner; Type 4 setup issue
Comparison article: expensive toner, Wi-Fi disconnects, high OEM cost per page; part numbers in it are wrong, so only general remarks used
